question: What regulatory body oversees nursing practice and professional conduct in Nigeria?

options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body charged with regulating nursing education and practice in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why is ignorance of the law not an accepted defense if a nurse makes a professional error?

options.A: The court assumes all nurses have a formal law degree
options.B: Hospital management takes full legal blame instead
options.C: Nurses are legally bound to know and follow professional standards
options.D: Ignorance is automatically classified as a criminal felony

explanation: Professional licensure requires practitioners to stay informed and compliant with laws governing their scope of practice. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which agency is primarily responsible for regulating the manufacture and distribution of drugs in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control

explanation: NAFDAC is mandated to regulate and control the manufacture, importation, and sale of drugs in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the primary role of the Pharmacists Council of Nigeria?

options.B: Arresting illegal drug hawkers on the streets
options.C: Regulating pharmacy practice and training standards
options.D: Issuing licenses to general hospital nurses

explanation: The PCN oversees the education, registration, and professional conduct of pharmacists and pharmacy technicians. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the standard temperature range for storing refrigerated medications?

options.A: Minus 5 degrees Celsius to 0 degrees Celsius

explanation: Maintaining cold chain integrity requires keeping specific biologicals and vaccines within 2°C to 8°C. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h3)

question: How should medications that are sensitive to light be stored on the ward?

options.A: Placed directly under bright fluorescent ward lights
options.B: Stored in opaque or amber packaging to block light
options.C: Exposed to sunlight daily to activate the chemical formula
options.D: Kept in clear glass containers for easy visual counting

explanation: Light-sensitive drugs degrade when exposed to ultraviolet or visible light, losing therapeutic efficacy. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h3)

question: How many core rights make up the traditional safety framework for giving medications?
explanation: The classic five rights cover patient, drug, dose, route, and time to minimize medication errors. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h4)

question: A nurse prepares an injection but is called away to an emergency before giving it. What is the correct action to take?

options.A: Leave the syringe on the patient's bedside table for later use
options.B: Discard the medication immediately and document the wastage
options.C: Keep the drug secure and administer it personally after the emergency
options.D: Hand the prepared drug to a ward assistant to administer

explanation: Medications must remain under the direct control of the administering clinician until given to the patient to prevent contamination or mix-ups. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h4)

question: What legal rule applies to charting medications on a patient's treatment sheet?

options.A: Verbal charting is legally equivalent to written charts
options.B: Charting can be delayed until the end of the week
options.C: Erasing mistakes is encouraged to keep charts clean
options.D: If it was not charted, it was not done

explanation: Courts and regulatory bodies rely strictly on contemporaneous written records as proof that care was delivered. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h5)

question: Why is backdating a missed medication entry on a chart a serious problem?

options.A: It increases the financial billing cost for the patient
options.B: It uses up too many pages in the patient treatment sheet
options.C: It falsifies official clinical records and misleads healthcare teams
options.D: It causes confusion with pharmacy inventory restocking counts

explanation: Altering the timeline of clinical documentation compromises the integrity of the medical record and misleads subsequent caregivers. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h5)

question: Where must dangerous and controlled substances be stored in a hospital ward?

options.A: Inside an unlocked refrigerator in the utility room
options.B: In a secure double-locked metal safe
options.C: On top of the open nurses' work station desk
options.D: Inside the general patient bedside medication locker

explanation: Controlled drugs require dual-lock security to prevent theft, diversion, and unauthorized access. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why must a second nurse witness when a controlled drug is given or wasted?

options.A: To ensure accountability and prevent drug diversion
options.B: To confirm the patient has medical insurance coverage
options.C: To sign the hospital financial billing ledger afterward
options.D: To help calculate the correct pediatric dosage conversion

explanation: Independent dual-witnessing provides an essential check against narcotic theft and undocumented wastage. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h6)

question: What happens legally if a nurse deliberately covers up a medication error?

options.A: It automatically clears the nurse of any disciplinary hearing
options.B: It reduces the financial penalty payable to the hospital board
options.C: It intensifies professional liability and constitutes gross negligence
options.D: It transfers the legal blame directly to the hospital pharmacist

explanation: Covering up an error shows intent to deceive, which severely aggravates legal and professional disciplinary penalties. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h7)

question: What should a nurse do immediately after realizing a wrong medication was given to a patient?

options.A: Assess the patient and notify the attending physician
options.B: Discharge the patient to avoid legal complications
options.C: Quietly correct the drug chart without telling anyone
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to inform management

explanation: Patient safety is the immediate priority, requiring clinical assessment and prompt medical intervention before documentation. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h7)

question: What legal charge can a nurse face for giving treatment to an adult patient who clearly refused it?
explanation: Touching a patient or administering treatment without lawful consent or after explicit refusal constitutes the tort of battery. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h8)

question: Which of the following explains patient autonomy regarding medications?

options.A: The right of a competent patient to accept or refuse treatment
options.B: The obligation of the nurse to force compliance with therapy
options.C: The authority of the doctor to prescribe without explanation
options.D: The power of the hospital board to overrule family wishes

explanation: Autonomy grants individuals the legal and moral right to make independent decisions about their own healthcare. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h8)
